blocks.text: Śiva Sūtras 3.34
blocks.directed: [long pause] Śiva Sūtras 3.34

blocks.text: तद्विमुक्तस्तु केवली
blocks.directed: [slowly] तद्विमुक्तस्तु केवली

blocks.text: Tadvimuktas tu kevalī.
blocks.directed: Tadvimuktas tu kevalī.

blocks.text: But the one liberated from those is kevalī — established in their own pure, independent nature.
blocks.directed: But the one liberated from those is kevalī — established in their own pure, independent nature.

blocks.text: Congratulations, You’re Alone. Not Lonely. Metaphysically Alone.
blocks.directed: Congratulations, You’re Alone. Not Lonely. Metaphysically Alone.

blocks.text: Now this is absolutely magnificent.
blocks.directed: Now this is absolutely magnificent.

blocks.text: Because we’ve just learned that the yogi can experience pleasure and pain without identifying their deepest nature with either.
blocks.directed: Because we’ve just learned that the yogi can experience pleasure and pain without identifying their deepest nature with either.

blocks.text: And Vasugupta immediately announces:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And Vasugupta immediately announces:

blocks.text: Kevalī.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Kevalī.

blocks.text: The one who stands alone.
blocks.directed: The one who stands alone.

blocks.text: Oh dear.
blocks.directed: Oh dear.

blocks.text: That sounds rather depressing.
blocks.directed: That sounds rather depressing.

blocks.text: You’ve attained the highest spiritual realization imaginable, and apparently there’s nobody else at the party.
blocks.directed: You’ve attained the highest spiritual realization imaginable, and apparently there’s nobody else at the party.

blocks.text: Just you.
blocks.directed: Just you.

blocks.text: And Śiva.
blocks.directed: And Śiva.

blocks.text: Who is also you.
blocks.directed: Who is also you.

blocks.text: And the entire universe.
blocks.directed: And the entire universe.

blocks.text: Which is also the manifestation of your own Śakti.
blocks.directed: Which is also the manifestation of your own Śakti.

blocks.text: What an extraordinarily confusing social gathering.
blocks.directed: What an extraordinarily confusing social gathering.

blocks.text: But let’s unpack the Sanskrit.
blocks.directed: But let’s unpack the Sanskrit.

blocks.text: Tad — those; referring to pleasure and pain.
blocks.directed: Tad — those; referring to pleasure and pain.

blocks.text: Vimuktaḥ — released, liberated, freed.
blocks.directed: Vimuktaḥ — released, liberated, freed.

blocks.text: Tu — but, indeed, marking a distinction.
blocks.directed: Tu — but, indeed, marking a distinction.

blocks.text: Kevalī — one established in aloneness, purity, or independence.
blocks.directed: Kevalī — one established in aloneness, purity, or independence.

blocks.text: And here we need to understand kaivalya.
blocks.directed: And here we need to understand kaivalya.

blocks.text: Because this is a term that appears in multiple Indian philosophical traditions, but it doesn’t always mean the same thing.
blocks.directed: Because this is a term that appears in multiple Indian philosophical traditions, but it doesn’t always mean the same thing.

blocks.text: In classical Sāṃkhya-Yoga, kaivalya is associated with the isolation of puruṣa from prakṛti.
blocks.directed: In classical Sāṃkhya-Yoga, kaivalya is associated with the isolation of puruṣa from prakṛti.

blocks.text: The conscious principle is distinguished from the material processes with which it had been confused.
blocks.directed: The conscious principle is distinguished from the material processes with which it had been confused.

blocks.text: But Trika doesn’t accept that ultimate metaphysical separation.
blocks.directed: But Trika doesn’t accept that ultimate metaphysical separation.

blocks.text: Because for Trika, the world of manifestation is not fundamentally independent of Śiva.
blocks.directed: Because for Trika, the world of manifestation is not fundamentally independent of Śiva.

blocks.text: It’s Śiva’s own Śakti.
blocks.directed: It’s Śiva’s own Śakti.

blocks.text: So Kṣemarāja’s kevalī is not an isolated consciousness hiding from an independently existing universe.
blocks.directed: So Kṣemarāja’s kevalī is not an isolated consciousness hiding from an independently existing universe.

blocks.text: The yogi is established in the pure conscious nature of the Self, no longer bound by identification with the subtle body and its pleasure-pain experiences.
blocks.directed: The yogi is established in the pure conscious nature of the Self, no longer bound by identification with the subtle body and its pleasure-pain experiences.

blocks.text: And this is what makes the doctrine so subtle.
blocks.directed: And this is what makes the doctrine so subtle.

blocks.text: The yogi isn’t simply detached from objects because objects are horrible.
blocks.directed: The yogi isn’t simply detached from objects because objects are horrible.

blocks.text: The yogi recognises their fundamental conscious nature as not dependent upon those objects.
blocks.directed: The yogi recognises their fundamental conscious nature as not dependent upon those objects.

blocks.text: Now Kṣemarāja makes the point exceptionally strongly.
blocks.directed: Now Kṣemarāja makes the point exceptionally strongly.

blocks.text: The liberated yogi is not internally touched even by the residual impressions of pleasure and pain.
blocks.directed: The liberated yogi is not internally touched even by the residual impressions of pleasure and pain.

blocks.text: Saṃskāra.
blocks.directed: [slowly] Saṃskāra.

blocks.text: The latent impressions left by experience.
blocks.directed: The latent impressions left by experience.

blocks.text: And that’s interesting.
blocks.directed: And that’s interesting.

blocks.text: Because ordinary pleasure and pain don’t simply disappear the moment the immediate experience ends.
blocks.directed: Because ordinary pleasure and pain don’t simply disappear the moment the immediate experience ends.

blocks.text: They can leave tendencies.
blocks.directed: They can leave tendencies.

blocks.text: Memories.
blocks.directed: Memories.

blocks.text: Habits.
blocks.directed: Habits.

blocks.text: Expectations.
blocks.directed: Expectations.

blocks.text: A pleasant experience may produce desire for repetition.
blocks.directed: A pleasant experience may produce desire for repetition.

blocks.text: A painful experience may produce aversion.
blocks.directed: A painful experience may produce aversion.

blocks.text: And the individual becomes governed by those residual dispositions.
blocks.directed: And the individual becomes governed by those residual dispositions.

blocks.text: But Kṣemarāja describes a yogi whose true conscious identity is no longer bound by even those impressions.
blocks.directed: But Kṣemarāja describes a yogi whose true conscious identity is no longer bound by even those impressions.

blocks.text: Their nature is cinmātra.
blocks.directed: Their nature is cinmātra.

blocks.text: Pure consciousness.
blocks.directed: Pure consciousness.

blocks.text: Now this is a traditional description of the highest yogic condition, not a clinical claim that liberated persons become incapable of remembering painful experiences.
blocks.directed: Now this is a traditional description of the highest yogic condition, not a clinical claim that liberated persons become incapable of remembering painful experiences.

blocks.text: And it certainly shouldn’t be used to deny someone’s suffering.
blocks.directed: And it certainly shouldn’t be used to deny someone’s suffering.

blocks.text: The distinction is between the functioning of experience and the ultimate identity of the experiencer.
blocks.directed: The distinction is between the functioning of experience and the ultimate identity of the experiencer.

blocks.text: Kṣemarāja invokes the Kālikākrama, which describes the yogi breaking through the great delusion of duality constructed through the cognitions of pleasure, pain and related mental states.
blocks.directed: Kṣemarāja invokes the Kālikākrama, which describes the yogi breaking through the great delusion of duality constructed through the cognitions of pleasure, pain and related mental states.

blocks.text: The problem is not simply that an unpleasant event occurs.
blocks.directed: The problem is not simply that an unpleasant event occurs.

blocks.text: It’s the metaphysical misunderstanding through which the limited cognitive subject is mistaken for the ultimate Self. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.
blocks.directed: It’s the metaphysical misunderstanding through which the limited cognitive subject is mistaken for the ultimate Self. Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism.

blocks.text: Now here’s the extraordinary point.
blocks.directed: Now here’s the extraordinary point.

blocks.text: Kevalī doesn’t mean a lonely individual.
blocks.directed: Kevalī doesn’t mean a lonely individual.

blocks.text: It means the yogi is no longer fundamentally dependent on the limitations that define individual subjectivity.
blocks.directed: It means the yogi is no longer fundamentally dependent on the limitations that define individual subjectivity.

blocks.text: They’re established in the conscious reality from which the appearance of individuality proceeds.
blocks.directed: They’re established in the conscious reality from which the appearance of individuality proceeds.

blocks.text: And that reality is not empty of manifestation.
blocks.directed: And that reality is not empty of manifestation.

blocks.text: It’s the source of manifestation.
blocks.directed: It’s the source of manifestation.

blocks.text: So we’re not talking about a person who has become metaphysically stranded in an infinite void.
blocks.directed: So we’re not talking about a person who has become metaphysically stranded in an infinite void.

blocks.text: We’re talking about consciousness no longer mistaken for the limited forms appearing within it.
blocks.directed: We’re talking about consciousness no longer mistaken for the limited forms appearing within it.

blocks.text: Now imagine someone obsessed with maintaining a particular state of happiness.
blocks.directed: Now imagine someone obsessed with maintaining a particular state of happiness.

blocks.text: Every experience is evaluated according to whether it produces pleasure.
blocks.directed: Every experience is evaluated according to whether it produces pleasure.

blocks.text: They seek pleasant things.
blocks.directed: They seek pleasant things.

blocks.text: Avoid unpleasant things.
blocks.directed: Avoid unpleasant things.

blocks.text: And organise their entire lives around protecting the conditions of satisfaction.
blocks.directed: And organise their entire lives around protecting the conditions of satisfaction.

blocks.text: Which, to be fair, is a fairly accurate description of much ordinary human behaviour.
blocks.directed: Which, to be fair, is a fairly accurate description of much ordinary human behaviour.

blocks.text: But the difficulty is that pleasure and pain are changing phenomena.
blocks.directed: But the difficulty is that pleasure and pain are changing phenomena.

blocks.text: If your identity depends upon preserving pleasant experience, you’re vulnerable to every change in its conditions.
blocks.directed: If your identity depends upon preserving pleasant experience, you’re vulnerable to every change in its conditions.

blocks.text: The happiness arrives.
blocks.directed: The happiness arrives.

blocks.text: You cling to it.
blocks.directed: You cling to it.

blocks.text: The happiness disappears.
blocks.directed: The happiness disappears.

blocks.text: You suffer.
blocks.directed: You suffer.

blocks.text: Then you begin searching for another happiness.
blocks.directed: Then you begin searching for another happiness.

blocks.text: And the entire process continues.
blocks.directed: And the entire process continues.

blocks.text: But the kevalī, in Kṣemarāja’s account, has recognised a reality not exhausted by this sequence.
blocks.directed: But the kevalī, in Kṣemarāja’s account, has recognised a reality not exhausted by this sequence.

blocks.text: And that changes the meaning of freedom.
blocks.directed: And that changes the meaning of freedom.

blocks.text: Freedom is not simply obtaining permanent pleasant sensations.
blocks.directed: Freedom is not simply obtaining permanent pleasant sensations.

blocks.text: It’s the recognition of the conscious reality underlying changing sensations.
blocks.directed: It’s the recognition of the conscious reality underlying changing sensations.

blocks.text: And now comes the rather devastating contrast.
blocks.directed: And now comes the rather devastating contrast.

blocks.text: Because Vasugupta is about to show us the opposite condition.
blocks.directed: Because Vasugupta is about to show us the opposite condition.

blocks.text: The individual who has not recognised their true nature.
blocks.directed: The individual who has not recognised their true nature.

blocks.text: The one who remains absorbed in pleasure and pain.
blocks.directed: The one who remains absorbed in pleasure and pain.

blocks.text: The one whose activity is governed by ignorance.
blocks.directed: The one whose activity is governed by ignorance.

blocks.text: The one who keeps generating karma.
blocks.directed: The one who keeps generating karma.

blocks.text: In other words:
blocks.directed: [short pause] In other words:

blocks.text: The rest of us.
blocks.directed: The rest of us.

blocks.text: Lovely.
blocks.directed: [short pause] Lovely.
